subject: Re: Rate parity request + commit tier options
messages:
From: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@acme.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rate parity request + details on current offer

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. Before we run a pilot, procurement asked me to follow up on pricing. We have a competing proposal from one of the major API providers (they offered a per-token rate that effectively comes to $0.028/1k prompt tokens for our typical mix, with an annual commit and additional credits for first 3 months).

Can Redwood do rate parity on Hosted API per-token pricing if we agree to a 12-month commit? Alternatively, what commit tiers and effective blended rates could you offer so I can model migration economics?

A couple of details on our usage mix (monthly averages):
- 1.2B prompt tokens, 0.8B generated tokens
- 80% standard chat, 20% embedding/rerank
- Target latency p95 < 300ms for chat endpoints

Procurement also requested a formal quote and any required SOC2/infra evidence.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — they want pricing for the board review next week.

Best,
Miguel
Head of Platform
Acme Corporation

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rate parity request + details on current offer

Miguel — thanks for the details and the clear usage breakdown. Happy to run numbers and get you a formal quote. Quick summary of what I can do today:

- Draft a 12-month commit proposal with tiered per-token pricing and a blended effective rate (volume-weighted)
- Include migration tokens (1 month of estimated tokens) and a performance SLA on Hosted API (p95 target we discussed)
- Attach a short benchmark we ran against the same workload profile (redwood-vs-openai-benchmarks-20260708.csv) and an initial quote PDF for internal review.

I attached a preliminary quote (see attached PDF) — it assumes a 12-month commit at the volumes you shared and includes a 10% up-front credit. If you can share the competitor effective rate (confirming if $0.028/1k is correct for the prompt side), I can bring this to pricing and see if we can tighten the gap.

Two quick clarifying Qs:
1) Are the 1.2B prompt tokens / 0.8B generated tokens fixed monthly or seasonal?
2) Is the embedding workload billed to the same budget line or a separate teams’ cost center?

I’ll loop in Ben (Sales Ops) to make sure we include appropriate commercial levers.

Thanks — I’ll aim to return a revised quote by EOD tomorrow.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

Thanks Hannah. A few clarifications:
- The competitor effective is indeed around $0.028/1k prompt tokens for their mid-tier model (they stacked on a 5% volume discount after year 1).
- Usage is fairly steady month-to-month, with a ~10% Q4 spike.
- embeddings come out of the same central platform budget.

Procurement’s ask is simple: can Redwood match the competitor’s per-token economics on our contracted volumes, or present a plan that nets us the same or better blended spend across the year (including credits and SLAs)? They are also sensitive to long-term exit costs — any migration assistance would be a plus.

If you can provide a price-matched quote and SOC2 evidence, I can move this to legal/finance for a quick review.

Miguel

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2026 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Rate parity request + details on current offer

Hannah — thanks for the context. Short answer: we can get very close but not full parity at $0.028/1k on the prompt side without a deeper multi-year commit. Proposal:

1) 12-month commit (volume as provided): blended effective rate = $0.031/1k prompt tokens (includes 1 month migration tokens and 10% up-front credit).
2) 24-month commit: blended effective rate = $0.0285/1k prompt tokens + 2 months migration tokens + prioritized capacity during ramp windows.
3) Add-ons: SOC2 report (standard redacted version) + add-on for full artifact access (upon signed NDA).

We should include a migration assistance credit equal to one month of estimated spend and offer a 60-day SLA credit schedule for missed p95 targets. We avoid lowering list price below $0.03/1k to protect channel economics, but the blended numbers above incorporate credits and token allowances that make the economics comparable.

If Acme needs a formal doc to sign quickly, produce a 24-month optional quote (sign now for 12-month, convert to 24-month with amendment within 60 days) — that gives them the price improvement path.

I will draft language for legal on exit/migration assistance and the SLA credit terms.

—Ben
VP, Sales Operations
Ben Carter
